source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Wheels and Tires, p.10-7

procedures.title: Tubeless tire: remove from rim
steps: Flip the tire; with two irons, pry the rim up with one between flange and bead, and pry outward with the other between bead seat and bead.

procedures.title: Tubeless tire: install on rim
steps: Wipe a thin film of Ruglyde or similar rubber lubricant on the tire sealing bead.
Mount the outer bead with tire irons in small bites around the rim, without harming the bead.
Mount the inner bead the same way.
If air rushes out and the bead will not seal, cinch a tire mounting band or heavy sash cord around the tire's circumference, tightening with a tire iron.
On a tire machine, lift the tire on the rim so the top bead is pushed against the top flange; the tire's weight seats the bottom bead.
notes: Too much lubricant can let the tire slip on the rim and break the air seal.
Caution: do not use a hammer; it will damage the bead.
Take great care not to damage the sealing bead and circumferential bead while forcing the tire over the rim.

procedures.title: Valve assembly: replace
steps: Coat the outside of the new valve generously with mounting compound.
Push it through the rim from the inside and snap it home with slip-joint pliers, one jaw on the rim and one on the valve base (the manual cites figure 7; figure 6 shows the valve being installed).
notes: The manual numbers these steps 4 and 5; no step 3 is printed.

procedures.title: Rim: repair
steps: Clean the flange well with a small piece of steel wool or sandpaper.
Check the butt weld in the flange area for any groove or high spot (the manual cites figure 8; figure 7 shows rim inspection at the butt weld).
If air leaks at the valve, replace the valve core or the whole valve assembly.
